title: Objective-C Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: printf is a C printing function. This Objective-C file can still use ordinary C code.

examples.title: Keep a whole number
examples.description: An int stores a whole number. %d tells printf where to place it.

examples.title: Use an NSString
examples.description: NSString is an object holding text. The @ before the quotes makes an Objective-C string object.

examples.title: Send a message to an object
examples.description: Square brackets send a message. length asks a string for its length in UTF-16 units.

examples.title: Build a string with a value
examples.description: stringWithFormat makes text with inserted values. %@ inserts an object description.

examples.title: Read an array item
examples.description: NSArray stores object values in order. The first index is zero.

examples.title: Find a value by key
examples.description: NSDictionary connects keys to values. A text key can describe the data.

examples.title: Choose a message
examples.description: Objective-C keeps C if statements. The comparison produces a true-or-false result.

examples.title: Visit each object
examples.description: Fast enumeration visits each object in a collection using for-in.

examples.title: Add an object
examples.description: NSMutableArray allows changes such as adding an object.

examples.title: Recognise no object
examples.description: nil means no object. Checking it can select a fallback message.

examples.title: Compare the text itself
examples.description: isEqualToString compares string contents. Pointer equality asks whether two references point to one object.
